title: Contract-Driven API Service Engineering
centralQuestion: Which application, database, worker, storage, and release mechanisms keep the public contract true under concurrency, restart, and partial failure?
responsibility: Turn the fixed Course 1 contract into a durable modular service whose important guarantees survive concurrent requests and process failure.
incomingBoundary: The immutable Course 1 API 1.1 handoff and its provider-neutral proof corpus.
outgoingBoundary: A durable API 1.2 service with migrations 001–005, persistent idempotency, atomic conditional updates, stable pagination, worker recovery, artifact integrity, transactional webhook delivery, and compatible-release evidence.
versionState: API 1.1 preserved; additive API 1.2 introduced; OpenAPI 3.1.2 preserved; migrations 001–005.
languageStrategy: one primary implementation track plus one comparative reference track

modules.title: Application Use Cases and Boundaries
modules.centralQuestion: How does a public operation become an application use case without letting the framework own the system?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Create transport, application, and adapter boundaries for the fixed operation ledger.
learningOutcomes: Separate transport, application, domain, and infrastructure responsibilities
Translate public models into internal commands and results
Inject clocks, identifiers, and external dependencies
Keep business decisions out of FastAPI and Fastify handlers
Map every operation ID to one application owner

modules.title: Domain State and Invariants
modules.centralQuestion: Which state transitions and invariants must remain true regardless of framework or database?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement project, dataset, run, cancellation, and artifact rules as testable domain behavior.
learningOutcomes: Model legal and illegal state transitions
Distinguish entities, values, commands, and outcomes pragmatically
Keep domain failures stable and transport-neutral
Control time and identifiers in tests
Prove invariants with pure state-transition tests

modules.title: Relational Modeling and Migrations
modules.centralQuestion: How should relational structure and migrations reinforce rather than merely store application invariants?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Persist principals, projects, datasets, runs, artifacts, and ownership with constraints and deterministic migrations.
learningOutcomes: Map relationships and ownership to keys and constraints
Use nullability and checks to exclude invalid states
Choose indexes from actual query patterns
Own migrations explicitly and apply them from an empty database
Map rows to domain objects without leaking persistence shape

modules.title: Transactions, Concurrency, ETags, and Idempotency
modules.centralQuestion: How do idempotency and conditional updates remain atomic under concurrent requests and process restarts?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement persistent request fingerprints, replayed outcomes, version columns, ETags, and transaction rollback.
learningOutcomes: Draw the transaction boundary for each use case
Implement compare-and-swap for `If-Match`
Persist idempotency scope, fingerprint, and response
Handle simultaneous duplicate requests with one logical winner
Prove rollback leaves no partial state

modules.title: Queries, Stable Pagination, and Authorized Access
modules.centralQuestion: How do filters, stable cursors, and authorization-aware queries remain correct while data changes?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement owner-bound, filter-bound, high-water keyset traversal and evidence-backed query plans.
learningOutcomes: Bind queries to principal, operation, filters, and order
Use opaque server-side cursor handles
Prevent duplicates and omissions during a traversal
Conceal foreign-resource existence where policy requires it
Read query plans and index use

modules.title: Durable Workers and Recovery
modules.centralQuestion: What makes a 202 Accepted operation honest after the API process or worker dies?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Add durable jobs, leases, heartbeats, fencing, cancellation, duplicate-safe effects, and abandoned-work recovery.
learningOutcomes: Separate durable acceptance from execution
Claim work without holding a long transaction
Fence stale workers with lease generation
Recover abandoned jobs safely
Make duplicate execution converge on one durable outcome

modules.title: Streaming and Artifact Integrity
modules.centralQuestion: How can large uploads, progress streams, and artifacts remain bounded, durable, and integrity-checked?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Implement streamed upload, content-addressed publication, checksums, SSE/NDJSON progress, and authorized download.
learningOutcomes: Enforce limits while streaming rather than after buffering
Stage bytes safely and clean up failures
Use content addressing and no-clobber publication
Persist event streams for SSE and NDJSON consumers
Keep artifact authorization and storage paths separate

modules.title: Transactional Outbox and Webhook Delivery
modules.centralQuestion: How can a committed business change reliably produce an external webhook without a dual write?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Add a transactional outbox, signed deliveries, retry state, deduplication, and destination constraints.
learningOutcomes: Explain the dual-write failure
Insert outbox intent in the domain transaction
Separate dispatcher attempts from logical events
Retry only classified failures with bounded delay
Require receiver deduplication for at-least-once delivery

modules.title: Failure-Oriented Verification
modules.centralQuestion: How do tests prove transactions, concurrency, restart, storage, and delivery guarantees rather than only happy paths?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Assemble pure, integration, concurrent, process-kill, conformance, and planted-defect proofs.
learningOutcomes: Choose the narrowest oracle for each claim
Use real PostgreSQL for database concurrency claims
Inject failures at transaction and process boundaries
Retain planted defects as regression tests
Separate deterministic local checks from environment-backed checks

modules.title: Lifecycle and Compatible Release
modules.centralQuestion: How can old and new service versions coexist through a database change and still preserve the public contract?
modules.capstoneIncrement: Build lifecycle controls, compatible expand/backfill/enforce migrations, rollback evidence, and release proof.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish startup, liveness, readiness, and draining
Order application and schema releases safely
Keep old and new service versions compatible during expansion
Define the rollback boundary explicitly
Release API 1.2 without breaking API 1.1 consumers
